title: Unsupported HTML tag in ABAP Doc
shortDescription: Reports tag-like tokens in ABAP Doc which are not ABAP Doc HTML tags.
extendedInformation:
ABAP Doc is parsed as HTML, a field symbol or a placeholder written as <name> is an
unsupported and unclosed tag, the system warns and the rendered documentation drops the word.

Supported tags are p, em, strong, ul, ol, li, br, h1, h2 and h3, also as closing tags and with attributes.

Write <name> to show the angle brackets. A "<" which is not followed by a letter, like "a < b", is not reported.

Only checks ABAP Doc inside class definitions and interfaces.

title: ABAP Doc line starting with @
shortDescription: Reports ABAP Doc lines starting with "@" which is not followed by a command.
extendedInformation:
In ABAP Doc, "@" at the start of a line introduces a command, the commands are
@parameter, @raising and @exception. Any other text after a leading "@", like a CDS annotation,
gives the syntax warning 'A command was expected after ABAP Doc symbol "@"'.

An "@" in the middle of a line is plain text and not reported.

Only checks ABAP Doc inside class definitions and interfaces.

title: ABAP Doc parameter names
shortDescription: Checks that the parameters documented in ABAP Doc exist in the method definition.
extendedInformation:
Reports "! @parameter lines in the ABAP Doc block in front of a METHODS or CLASS-METHODS
definition when the parameter is not a parameter of the method, typically after a parameter was renamed or removed.
Also reports a parameter documented twice.

Missing @parameter lines are not reported, documenting parameters is optional. @raising and @exception lines are not checked.

Only the block directly in front of the method is checked, a blank line or a plain comment ends the block,
see rule wrong_abapdoc_position for misplaced ABAP Doc.

title: Alias never reassigned
shortDescription: Finds DATA(a) = b. where neither a nor b changes afterwards, so b can be read instead of a
extendedInformation:
Reports DATA(a) = b. when all of the following hold:

* a is a local variable of a METHOD, FORM or FUNCTION, and has at least two more references, all of them reads,
  which do not take its address, bind a field symbol to it, or pass it to USING, CHANGING or EXPORTING
* b is a local variable, or a component of one, whose address is never taken and which is not written
  after the declaration of a; or b is a constant or me
* the declaration is executed before every read on every path: each read is in the block of the declaration
  or a nested block

a has the type of b, so reading b instead does not change any conversion.
A constant b read in IF, ELSEIF, WHILE, CHECK, CASE or WHEN is not reported, see constant_condition.
Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL.

The quick fix deletes the declaration and replaces every read of a with b. No release requirement.

See also unnecessary_copy for copies that are read once, also of attributes and parameters.

title: Boolean flag via IF
shortDescription: Finds a flag that is initialized to false and set to true in a single IF, use xsdbool
extendedInformation:
Reports DATA(f) = VALUE abap_bool( )., DATA(f) = abap_false. or DATA f TYPE abap_bool.,
later followed by IF cond. f = abap_true. ENDIF., when all of the following hold:

* f is a local variable of a METHOD, FORM or FUNCTION, of type c LENGTH 1, its address is never taken
* the IF has no ELSEIF and no ELSE, its only statement is f = abap_true. and it contains no comments
* f has no other write, and is not read before the IF
* the IF is in the same block and the same loop as the declaration; DATA f TYPE abap_bool. is not
  executed per loop iteration, so neither it nor the IF may be in a loop

Requires xsdbool, ie. 7.40 SP08 or above, ABAP Cloud or open-abap.
Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL.

The quick fix deletes an inline declaration and replaces the IF with DATA(f) = xsdbool( cond ).,
or keeps DATA f TYPE abap_bool. and replaces the IF with f = xsdbool( cond ).

use_bool_expression covers IF with an ELSE branch, without looking at the declaration and the other uses.

title: Bound check after create
shortDescription: Finds IF r IS BOUND / IS NOT BOUND directly after r was created
extendedInformation:
Reports IF r IS BOUND. and IF r IS NOT BOUND. after CREATE OBJECT r., r = NEW ...( ). or
DATA(r) = NEW ...( ). in the same block, when all of the following hold:

* r is a local variable whose address is never taken, or an attribute: attr, me->attr or local->attr
* CREATE OBJECT has no EXCEPTIONS addition and no dynamic type, NEW is not followed by a method call
* every statement in between is a direct statement of the same block, not a nested structure
* a local r is not written in between
* for an attribute: no method, function or form call and no constructor in between, the local before ->
  is not written, and no write in between can change the attribute: no write to an attribute with the
  same name, to a field symbol, via ->*, or to a parameter passed by reference

The quick fix keeps the IS BOUND branch and removes the rest, or removes the IS NOT BOUND branch;
nothing is reported if a removed branch declares data that is used outside of it.
Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL. No release requirement.

title: Cast via generic reference
shortDescription: Finds a down cast from a local reference variable that only holds a copy of another reference
extendedInformation:
Reports DATA o TYPE REF TO object. o = r. ... x ?= o. when all of the following hold:

* o is a local variable of a METHOD, FORM or FUNCTION, declared with DATA without VALUE and not chained,
  typed REF TO object, or REF TO a class or interface that is the static type of r or a supertype of it
* o has exactly one write, o = r., exactly one read, the complete source of x ?= o., and its address is never
  taken. x is not an inline declaration
* r is a plain object reference: a variable, or a chain of attributes and components without calls,
  offsets, table expressions, field symbols or ->*
* r keeps its value from o = r. until the read, as in unnecessary_copy: for a local r, no write to it and its
  address is never taken; for other r, in addition no method, function or form call and no write except to
  local variables, by value parameters and RETURNING in between
* o = r. is executed before x ?= o. on every path: the read is in the same block or a nested block, and both
  are in the same loop
* x ?= r. is valid: x or r is typed REF TO object or an interface, or the class of x and the class of r
  are in the same inheritance line

The object is the same, so the cast succeeds or raises cx_sy_move_cast_error the same way.
try_cast_empty_catch can then replace a TRY around the cast.
Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL.

The quick fix deletes the declaration and o = r., and casts r directly. No release requirement.

title: Line of a sorted or hashed table passed to CHANGING
shortDescription: A field symbol on a whole line of a sorted or hashed table, passed to a CHANGING parameter of a method
extendedInformation:
The key fields of a sorted or hashed table line are write-protected, so the line as a whole is
write-protected. Binding it to a CHANGING parameter activates, but the call fails at runtime with
CX_SY_DYN_CALL_ILLEGAL_TYPE, "the actual parameter for ... is write-protected", even when the method does not
change the key.

Only field symbols assigned in the same method, form or function module are checked, via READ TABLE ... ASSIGNING,
LOOP AT ... ASSIGNING, INSERT ... INTO TABLE ... ASSIGNING and ASSIGN itab[ ... ] TO.

Fix: read the line into a work area, pass the work area and MODIFY TABLE ... FROM it afterwards,
or pass only the non-key fields the method needs.

title: CLEAR after declaration
shortDescription: Finds CLEAR of a local variable that is still initial since its declaration
extendedInformation:
Reports CLEAR x. when all of the following hold:

* x is a local variable of a METHOD, FORM or FUNCTION, declared with DATA x TYPE/LIKE ... without VALUE,
  or with DATA(x) = VALUE t( ). with an explicit type and nothing in the parentheses
* the CLEAR is the first reference to x after the declaration, it has no WITH addition
* neither the declaration nor the CLEAR is inside a LOOP, DO, WHILE, SELECT loop, PROVIDE, or a TRY block with
  RETRY, RESUME or CATCH BEFORE UNWIND. DATA is not executed per iteration, so a CLEAR in a loop can be needed.
  DATA(x) = VALUE t( ). is executed per iteration, it may also be in the same loop as the CLEAR, if the CLEAR is
  in the block of the declaration or a nested block

Any later use of x does not matter, the CLEAR can only be reached with x still initial.
Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL.

The quick fix deletes the CLEAR. No release requirement.

title: CLEAR before overwrite
shortDescription: Finds CLEAR of a local variable whose next use overwrites it completely
extendedInformation:
Reports CLEAR v. when all of the following hold:

* v is a local variable of a METHOD, FORM or FUNCTION, its address is never taken: no field symbol,
  REF #( ), GET REFERENCE, and it is not passed to a parameter by reference
* the CLEAR is not chained and has no WITH addition
* the next reference to v is a full overwrite in the same block: v = <expression>., including v = NEW ...,
  or CREATE OBJECT v. with optional TYPE and EXPORTING, where nothing else in the statement references v.
  Not ?=, READ TABLE INTO, offset/length or component writes, CREATE OBJECT with EXCEPTIONS, or other
  statements that can leave v unchanged
* every statement between the CLEAR and the overwrite is a direct statement of the block, not a nested structure,
  and does not reference v
* v is not a table with header line
* if a TRY or CATCH SYSTEM-EXCEPTIONS encloses the CLEAR, nothing from the CLEAR to the overwrite can raise
  an exception, a CATCH could see the old value: the overwrite directly follows the CLEAR and assigns a variable
  or a literal of identical type, or a reference variable

Unlike clear_after_declaration, the CLEAR can be in a loop.
Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL.

The quick fix deletes the CLEAR. No release requirement.

title: Clear EXPORTING parameters
shortDescription: Checks that EXPORTING parameters passed by reference are cleared or assigned before they are read
extendedInformation:
An EXPORTING parameter passed by reference behaves like a CHANGING parameter: it is not
initialized when the method is called, so it can still contain a value supplied by the caller. Clear or overwrite it
before reading it, so a leftover value is not accidentally used.

https://github.com/SAP/styleguides/blob/main/clean-abap/CleanABAP.md#clear-or-overwrite-exporting-reference-parameters

https://help.sap.com/doc/abapdocu_latest_index_htm/latest/en-US/abenref_transf_output_param_guidl.html

Note: EXPORTING parameters passed by VALUE are always initialized and are therefore not reported.
Reading and writing the parameter in the same statement (e.g. "ev_result = ev_result + 1") is reported,
as the source is evaluated before the parameter is assigned.
Objects containing parser or syntax errors are not reported.
"IS SUPPLIED"/"IS REQUESTED" checks are not considered reads, and "GET REFERENCE OF" plus
"ASSIGN ... TO <fs>" are considered writes, as the value can be written via the reference.

Class and interface method implementations and function modules are checked.

title: Constant condition
shortDescription: Finds IF and ELSEIF conditions on local variables whose value is known
extendedInformation:
Reports two cases, for local variables of a METHOD, FORM or FUNCTION.

1. DATA(c) = <constant>. where the constant is a character literal like 'X', or a character constant like
abap_true, abap_false or space, and the only other reference to c is the condition of an IF or ELSEIF:
c = <constant>, c <> <constant>, EQ, NE, c IS INITIAL, c IS NOT INITIAL, optionally with NOT.
The declaration must be executed before the condition on every path: the IF is in the block of the
declaration or a nested block. The quick fix deletes the declaration.

2. DATA v TYPE ... without VALUE, or DATA(v) = VALUE t( ). with an explicit type and nothing in the parentheses,
where v is never changed, except by CLEAR v., and its address is never taken, in a condition v IS [NOT] INITIAL
or v IS [NOT] BOUND. The declaration is kept.

The quick fix removes the IF branch that is never taken, or keeps the branch that is always taken and
removes the rest, also in ELSEIF chains: a first IF branch that is never taken turns the next ELSEIF into IF,
an ELSEIF branch that is always taken turns into ELSE. Nothing is reported if a removed branch declares
data that is used outside of it.

Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL. No release requirement.

title: Copy chain
shortDescription: Finds a local variable that only passes a value on from one variable to another
extendedInformation:
Reports a local variable that only passes a value on, in two cases.

1. DATA v TYPE ... [CLEAR v.] v = src. ... y = v. when all of the following hold:

* v is a local variable of a METHOD, FORM or FUNCTION, declared with DATA without VALUE, or with
  DATA(v) = VALUE t( ). with an explicit type and nothing in the parentheses
* v has exactly one write besides CLEAR: v = src., and all CLEARs are before it
* v has exactly one read, the complete source of y = v.
* src is a local variable, or a pass-by-value or RETURNING parameter of a method or form, its address is never
  taken, and it is not written from v = src. until y = v.
* v = src. is executed before y = v. on every path: y = v. is in the same block or a nested block,
  and both are in the same loop
* v and src are both reference types, or have identical types; for other types the copy into v can convert,
  e.g. truncate a string into a c field. For DATA(y) = v. the types must be identical, else y changes its type
* the declaration, the CLEARs and v = src. are not chained

The quick fix deletes the declaration, the CLEARs and v = src., and changes the read to y = src.

2. DATA a TYPE REF TO c. CREATE OBJECT a. b = a. when all of the following hold:

* a is a local variable, declared with DATA without VALUE and not chained, its address is never taken
* the only other references to a are CREATE OBJECT a. and the complete source of b = a., which is the next
  statement in the same block, apart from declarations like DATA in between
* CREATE OBJECT has at most TYPE and EXPORTING, it is not chained. With EXCEPTIONS, a classic exception in the
  constructor would leave b unchanged instead of initial
* b is a local variable, or a pass-by-value or RETURNING parameter, whose address is never taken, it is
  declared before the CREATE OBJECT and not used in its parameters, so the constructor cannot see b
* b = a. passes the syntax check, so the static type of b accepts the class of a

The quick fix deletes the declaration of a and b = a., and creates the object in b, keeping TYPE and EXPORTING.
If the static types of a and b differ, it adds TYPE with the class of a.

Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL. No release requirement.

title: Copy of initial variable
shortDescription: Finds assignments from a local variable that is always initial
extendedInformation:
Reports DATA v TYPE ... [CLEAR v.] x = v. when all of the following hold:

* v is a local variable of a METHOD, FORM or FUNCTION, declared with DATA without VALUE, or with
  DATA(v) = VALUE t( ). with an explicit type and nothing in the parentheses. Both make v initial, the latter
  every time it is executed, so v is initial wherever it is read, also in loops
* v is never changed, except by CLEAR v., and its address is never taken
* v has exactly one read, the complete source of x = v., where x is not an inline declaration
* x and v are both reference types, or have identical types. Initial values convert differently between
  types, e.g. an initial d becomes '00000000' in a string
* the declaration and the CLEARs are not chained

Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL.

The quick fix deletes the declaration and the CLEARs, and replaces x = v. with CLEAR x.
No release requirement.

title: DELETE INDEX sy-tabix inside a LOOP over the same table
shortDescription: Reports DELETE itab INDEX sy-tabix inside a LOOP AT the same table
extendedInformation:
sy-tabix is the index of the loop's current row only until another statement writes it.
READ TABLE, APPEND, INSERT, COLLECT, a nested LOOP and any method called in the loop body
all set sy-tabix. After that the DELETE removes a different row, and if sy-tabix is 0 it
raises the runtime error TABLE_INVALID_INDEX.

Use DELETE itab WHERE ..., or collect the rows to keep in a second table.

Not reported: DELETE itab INDEX sy-tabix directly after READ TABLE itab, where sy-tabix
is the index the READ just set.

title: Downport statement
shortDescription: Downport functionality
extendedInformation:
Much like the 'commented_code' rule this rule loops through unknown statements and tries parsing with
a higher level language version. If successful, various rules are applied to downport the statement.
Target downport version is always v702, thus rule is only enabled if target version is v702.

Current rules:
* NEW transformed to CREATE OBJECT, opposite of https://rules.abaplint.org/use_new/
* DATA() definitions are outlined, opposite of https://rules.abaplint.org/prefer_inline/
* FIELD-SYMBOL() definitions are outlined
* CONV is outlined
* COND is outlined
* REDUCE is outlined
* SWITCH is outlined
* FILTER is outlined
* APPEND expression is outlined
* INSERT expression is outlined
* EMPTY KEY is changed to DEFAULT KEY, opposite of DEFAULT KEY in https://rules.abaplint.org/avoid_use/
* CAST changed to ?=
* LOOP AT method_call( ) is outlined
* VALUE # with structure fields
* VALUE # with internal table lines
* Table Expressions are outlined
* SELECT INTO @DATA definitions are outlined
* Some occurrences of string template formatting option ALPHA changed to function module call
* SELECT/INSERT/MODIFY/DELETE/UPDATE "," in field list removed, "@" in source/targets removed
* PARTIALLY IMPLEMENTED removed, it can be quick fixed via rule implement_methods
* RAISE EXCEPTION ... MESSAGE
* Moving with +=, -=, /=, *=, &&= is expanded
* line_exists and line_index is downported to READ TABLE
* ENUMs, but does not nessesarily give the correct type and value
* MESSAGE with non simple source

Only one transformation is applied to a statement at a time, so multiple steps might be required to do the full downport.

Make sure to test the downported code, it might not always be completely correct.

title: IS ASSIGNED after READ TABLE or ASSIGN in a loop
shortDescription: Reports IS [NOT] ASSIGNED after a READ TABLE ... ASSIGNING or ASSIGN inside a loop, without UNASSIGN before it
extendedInformation:
A failed READ TABLE ... ASSIGNING or ASSIGN keeps the previous binding of the field symbol. Inside a
loop, the field symbol still points to the row of an earlier iteration, so IS ASSIGNED is true
although the statement failed, and the code goes on with the wrong row.

Add UNASSIGN <fs> before the statement, inside the loop, or check sy-subrc after a READ TABLE.
The quick fix inserts the UNASSIGN; it is not offered for a field symbol declared inline in
the statement, or for a chained statement.

Not reported: a check that also reads sy-subrc, an ASSIGN that cannot fail (a static source
without dereference, table expression or dynamic part), and loops outside of the
method, form or function module of the statement. See also subrc_after_assign.

title: Prefer Inline CAST
shortDescription: Inline a CAST helper read only once in the next statement
extendedInformation:
Requires 7.40 SP02 or above, or ABAP Cloud, and no syntax errors.

Reports DATA(t) = CAST type( source ) when the helper has exactly one read and no other access,
except its declaration write, in the entire syntax scope (including earlier reads in loop bodies and exception handlers).
The immediately following statement must be a plain assignment, an attribute read, a receiver method call,
or a named IMPORTING argument of a functional method call (caller syntax p = t).

Only class/interface CAST targets, simple assignment targets and static access are supported.
For argument uses, the CAST operand must be a plain field chain without calls, the receiver and all
other arguments must be plain variables or literals, and the method signature must be known.
Explicit EXPORTING, IMPORTING and CHANGING sections are not supported.
Objects containing macros or dynamic access are skipped. Field symbols, reference-taking,
pragmas and chained statements are not supported.

Predicates such as IS INITIAL / IS BOUND and removal of statically redundant CASTs are left for a future version.

title: PREFERRED PARAMETER is ignored
shortDescription:
PREFERRED PARAMETER on an IMPORTING clause that still has a mandatory
parameter. The addition names the parameter a positional call fills, which only
means something when every parameter may be left out - so with a mandatory one
present it does nothing.
extendedInformation:
`PREFERRED PARAMETER` names the importing parameter that a call filling exactly
one parameter positionally fills. That question only arises when a parameter
may be LEFT OUT, so the addition is ignored while any importing parameter is
neither `OPTIONAL` nor carries a `DEFAULT`.

The compiler warns "Declare the parameter as OPTIONAL. The addition PREFERRED
PARAMETER is ignored if non-optional parameters are used", yet it still lets a
call leave the preferred parameter out. So the quick fix declares the mandatory
importing parameters OPTIONAL, as the compiler asks: every call that compiles
today keeps compiling. Removing the addition instead would turn the calls that
leave the preferred parameter out into syntax errors.

title: Range row values
shortDescription: Checks the SIGN and OPTION of range rows built with VALUE
extendedInformation:
A row of a range table, ie. a structure with exactly the components SIGN, OPTION, LOW and HIGH,
is a selection structure to the syntax check. For a VALUE row of one, the system warns when SIGN or OPTION
is missing, and when a literal is not a permitted value: SIGN must be I or E, OPTION one of
EQ NE BT NB CP NP GT GE LT LE, in upper case.

Components given in the VALUE header count for the rows that follow, eg. VALUE #( sign = 'I' option = 'EQ' ( low = 1 ) ).
Only literals are checked, a value from a variable, constant or expression is not.

title: Single use expression temporary
shortDescription: Finds a local variable that only passes the value of an expression on to its single use
extendedInformation:
Reports DATA(v) = <expression>. and DATA v TYPE t. [CLEAR v.] v = <expression>.
when all of the following hold:

* v is a local variable of a METHOD, FORM or FUNCTION, its address is never taken. DATA(v) has no other
  reference than its single read; DATA v TYPE t. without VALUE and not chained, or DATA(v) = VALUE t( ). with
  nothing in the parentheses, has exactly one write besides CLEARs, v = <expression>., all CLEARs are before it,
  and exactly one read after it
* the read is one of
  * the complete source of y = v.
  * the receiver of a method call or attribute access: v->m( ), v->attr
  * an actual parameter for an importing parameter: m( v ), m( p = v ), CALL METHOD m EXPORTING p = v,
    NEW c( p = v ) or CREATE OBJECT o EXPORTING p = v
  * APPEND v TO itab.
  * an operand of a comparison with =, <>, <, >, <=, >= or their word forms, in IF, ELSEIF or xsdbool( )
  * an embedding in a string template: |{ v }|
* the read is in the statement directly after the assignment, in the same block, ignoring declarations like
  DATA and TYPES in between, unless the expression is
  constant: a literal, a string template without embeddings, CONV t( <integer literal> ) to a type that cannot
  overflow, or a constant. Then the assignment must be executed before the read on every path: the read is in
  the block of the assignment or a nested block
* the result type of the expression does not depend on the target: no arithmetic or bit operators, no unary
  minus, no numeric functions like abs( ) or trunc( ) whose type follows the argument, no CONV or EXACT except
  the constant CONV t( literal ), no # type inference at the top. String templates, && concatenations, literals, method calls, NEW, CAST,
  constructor expressions with explicit type and table expressions are fine
* for DATA v TYPE t. and DATA(v) = VALUE t( )., the static type of the expression is identical to t. Into y = v. also a reference whose
  static type is a subtype of t, unless y is an inline declaration, and an expression whose type depends on the
  target, like arithmetic, if y has a type identical to t
* VALUE, CORRESPONDING, COND, SWITCH, REDUCE and FILTER can build their result directly in the target,
  they are only moved into a new variable, or a local variable that they do not read and whose address
  is never taken
* the order of evaluation does not change: if the expression is not constant, nothing that is evaluated before the
  read in the same statement calls a method or function, constructs an object, accesses a table or an attribute
  via a reference, does arithmetic, or reads data other than local variables, pass-by-value parameters and
  constants; the read is not inside COND, SWITCH, VALUE or other constructor expressions except NEW, and not
  after AND, OR or EQUIV, where it might not be evaluated. This does not apply to expressions that only read
  local variables and cannot raise an exception
* a data object that other code can change is only moved if it keeps its value until the read, see
  unnecessary_copy, a data object read by DATA(v) = <data object>. is left for unnecessary_copy, and a local
  variable copied into y = v. for copy_chain
* a character constant in IF, ELSEIF, WHILE, CHECK, CASE or WHEN is left for constant_condition

Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL.

The quick fix deletes the declaration, the CLEARs and the assignment, and replaces the read of v with the
expression. Moving the expression of DATA v TYPE t. into other places than y = v. requires 7.40 SP02 or above,
ABAP Cloud or open-abap.

title: SORT or DELETE ADJACENT DUPLICATES on a table with an empty key

extendedInformation:

The syntax check warns: "ITAB is a table with an empty primary key. Check the semantics of the statement."

Sorted and hashed tables, tables with a default or explicit key, and tables of unknown or generic type are not reported.

The quick fix adds BY table_line or COMPARING table_line, for tables with an elementary row type.

title: sy-subrc checked after ASSIGN
shortDescription: Reports a sy-subrc check directly after an ASSIGN, use IS [NOT] ASSIGNED instead
extendedInformation:
On a 7.40 SP7 system sy-subrc was still 4 after a successful ASSIGN, left over from an earlier
READ TABLE, see https://github.com/abap2UI5/abap2UI5/issues/1937. Current releases set sy-subrc here.
IS [NOT] ASSIGNED asks the field symbol directly and does not depend on the release.

A failed ASSIGN keeps the previous binding of the field symbol. So inside a loop, or when the
field symbol is bound earlier in the same method, IS ASSIGNED is true after a failed ASSIGN.
There, add UNASSIGN <fs> before the ASSIGN. The quick fix is only offered when the field symbol
is declared in the method, bound only by this ASSIGN, and the ASSIGN is not in a loop.

ASSIGN COMPONENT ... OF STRUCTURE is not reported.

title: TRY around cast with empty CATCH
shortDescription: Finds a down cast in TRY with an empty CATCH cx_sy_move_cast_error, use IS INSTANCE OF
extendedInformation:
Reports TRY. a ?= b. CATCH cx_sy_move_cast_error. ENDTRY. when all of the following hold:

* the cast is the only statement of the TRY block, there is exactly one CATCH, for cx_sy_move_cast_error only,
  without INTO or BEFORE UNWIND, its block is empty, and there is no CLEANUP
* the static type of a is a class or interface, not a generic REF TO object
* b is a plain data object: variable, attribute or a chain of components and attributes, without calls,
  so evaluating it again has no side effects

a ?= b. also succeeds when b is initial, and then clears a, while b IS INSTANCE OF is false for an initial b,
so the quick fix replaces the TRY with IF b IS INSTANCE OF <type of a> OR b IS INITIAL. a ?= b. ENDIF.

Requires IS INSTANCE OF, ie. 7.50 or above, ABAP Cloud or open-abap.
Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL.

title: Unnecessary copy
shortDescription: Finds DATA(a) = b. where a is read exactly once, and b can be read instead
extendedInformation:
Reports DATA(a) = b. when all of the following hold:

* a is a local variable of a METHOD, FORM or FUNCTION, and has exactly one more reference: a read,
  which does not take its address, bind a field symbol to it, or pass it to USING or CHANGING
* b is a plain data object: variable, constant, attribute, or a chain of components and attributes,
  without calls, offsets, table expressions, field symbols or ->*
* the declaration is executed before the read on every path: the read is in the block of the declaration
  or a nested block, and both are in the same loop
* b keeps its value from the declaration until the read: for a local b, or a pass-by-value or RETURNING
  parameter b of a method or form, no write to it and its address is never taken; for other b, in addition no
  method, function or form call and no write except to local variables, by value parameters and RETURNING in
  between, and in the statement of the read no call before the read. A method called in that statement could
  change b while it reads the parameter that b is passed to by reference, so the read may only be the receiver
  of the call, or the actual parameter of a pass-by-value parameter of the only method called in the statement

a has the type of b, so reading b instead does not change any conversion.
A constant b read in IF, ELSEIF, WHILE, CHECK, CASE or WHEN is not reported, see constant_condition.
Objects with syntax errors, macros or unknown statements are skipped, as are procedures with dynamic code,
INCLUDE, test seams, enhancements or native SQL.

The quick fix deletes the declaration and replaces the read of a with b. No release requirement,
inline declarations need 7.40 SP02 already.

See also alias_never_reassigned for copies that are read several times.

extendedInformation: SMIM and W3MI files are not checked.

title: Wrong ABAP Doc position
shortDescription: ABAP Doc must be placed directly in front of the declaration it documents.
extendedInformation:
ABAP Doc documents the single declaration following it, an ABAP Doc block placed
elsewhere is silently ignored, leaving the declaration undocumented.

The following positions are reported,
* in front of a chained keyword, ie. before "CONSTANTS:" instead of after the colon,
* in the middle of a statement, ie. between the parameters of a METHODS definition,
* directly in front of ENDCLASS, ENDINTERFACE or a SECTION statement,
* separated from its declaration by a blank line or a normal comment, the system reads both as the end of the block.

Only checks ABAP Doc inside class definitions and interfaces, and directly in front of them.

The quick fix for a blank line deletes the blank lines.

title: XML UTF-8 byte order mark
shortDescription: Checks that XML files start with a UTF-8 byte order mark
extendedInformation: Checks that each XML file has a UTF-8 byte order mark (BOM) at its beginning.

title: XML consistency
shortDescription: Checks the consistency of main XML files
extendedInformation:
Checks:
* XML is well-formed and parseable
* Naming for CLAS and INTF objects
* QUAN fields in TABL objects have reference table and field values
* Transparent TABL objects have delivery class and size category set
* TABL fields with a built-in type carry the INTTYPE abapGit serializes for it, for the confirmed pairs
* Lock parameter names in ENQU objects are max 16 characters
* Texts and translations do not exceed maximum allowed length.
